newsitem.title: UK: Saddam security services said moving into N.Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Saddam security services said moving into N.Iraq.

text.p: Saddam Hussein's security services have moved into northern Iraq, where one of two major Kurdish factions is in control after receiving support from Baghdad, an Iraqi opposition group said on Saturday.
The London-based Iraqi National Congress (INC) said senior officials from military intelligence and the public security services had been sent to the northern towns of Arbil, Dohuk and Suleymaniye.
"Officials from several of Saddam's brutal security services have moved to northern Iraq following Saddam's incursion," said the Iraqi Broadcasting Service, which is affiliated to the INC.

It said two regional directors of military intelligence had transferred their headquarters to Arbil and Dohuk respectively while the directors of the intelligence and public security services in Kirkuk had moved to Arbil.
"Reports also indicate that 30 agents of the public security service have entered Suleymaniye," it added.

On Monday the Baghdad-backed Kurdistan Democratic Party said it was in control of the whole of northern Iraq after capturing Arbil, the biggest city in the region, from the rival Patriotic Union of Kurdistan.
